'''Maximilian Haider''' (born 23 January 1950) is an [[Austria]]n [[physicist]] known for his contributions to [[Electron microscope|electron microscopy]]. He obtained the 2011 [[Wolf Prize in Physics]] and the 2020 [[Kavli Prize]] in Nanoscience for the development of the [[aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy]] in collaboration with [[Harald Rose]] and [[Knut Urban]].

== Biography ==
Maximilian Haider was born in Freistadt, Austria in 1950.

He studied physics at the [[University of Kiel]] and the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]], where he received his doctoral degree with a thesis entitled "Design, construction and testing of a corrected [[Electron energy loss spectroscopy|electron energy loss spectrometer]] with large dispersion and a large acceptance angle" (in German: "''Entwurf, Bau und Erprobung eines korrigierten Elektronen-Energieverlust-Spektrometers mit grosser Dispersion und grossem Akzeptanzwinkel''") in 1987. In 1989 he became Group Leader within the Physical Instrumentation Program at the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory]] (EMBL) where he had already performed some experiments during his doctoral studies.

He is honorary professor at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]] (KIT);<ref name="Jürgens">{{cite web | last=Jürgens | first=Michaela | title=LEM – Mitarbeiter | website=KIT | url=https://www.lem.kit.edu/21_139.php | language=de | access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref> co-founder, senior advisor and former president of [[Corrected Electron Optical Systems GmbH]] (CEOS), a German company that manufactures correction components for electron microscopes.<ref name="Corrected Electron Optical Systems">{{cite web | title=Dr. Max Haider | website=Corrected Electron Optical Systems | url=https://www.ceos-gmbh.de/de/ueber/max-haider | language=de | access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref>

== Honors ==

He won the 2011 [[Wolf Prize]] in Physics, along with [[Harald Rose]] and [[Knut Urban]], for his contributions to [[electron microscopy]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kit.edu/kit/english/pi_2011_7147.php|title=KIT – KIT – Media – Press Releases – Archive Press Releases – Maximilian Haider Is Granted Wolf Prize for Physics|date=16 April 2021|website=www.kit.edu|accessdate=14 December 2021}}</ref> specifically for the development of a device to correct electron-optical aberration using magnetic multipole lenses. Their work allowed electron microscopes to achieve a resolution of about 50 [[picometer|pm]], comparable to the [[Hydrogen atom|radius of the smallest atom]]. The three started working together in 1992. Haider built the first prototype and he is the founder (with Joachim Zach in 1996) of the German company [[Corrected Electron Optical Systems GmbH]] (CEOS), which manufactures and sells their invention.

In 2005 Haider, Zach and their company CEOS received the [[Dr.-Rudolf-Eberle Prize]] (Innovation prize from [[Baden-Württemberg]]).<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.ceos-gmbh.de/en/about/innovation |title = Innovation Award &#124; Corrected Electron Optical Systems}}</ref>

Haider, Rose and Urban also received the [[Karl-Heinz-Beckurts Prize]] in 2006 and the [[Honda Prize]] in 2008.<ref>[http://www.hondafoundation.jp/winner/view_en/406 Honda Prize Past Laureates]</ref>

In 2008 he became honorary professor at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]] (KIT).

A symposium on "Advances in Corrected Electron Microscopy in Materials Science and Biology" was held in honor of his 60th birthday on 19 February 2010 in [[Heidelberg]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.ceos-gmbh.de/en/about/congress |title = Congress in honour of Maximilian Haider and Harald Rose &#124; Corrected Electron Optical Systems}}</ref>

Haider also received the 2013 [[BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.fbbva.es/TLFU/tlfu/ing/microsites/premios/fronteras/galardonados/2013/ciencias.jsp |title=BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Awards |access-date=11 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151006111402/http://www.fbbva.es/TLFU/tlfu/ing/microsites/premios/fronteras/galardonados/2013/ciencias.jsp |archive-date=6 October 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> in Basic Sciences, along with [[Harald Rose]] and [[Knut Urban]], for greatly enhancing the resolving power of electron microscopy by developing aberration-corrected electron optics, a breakthrough enabling subatomic precision.

In 2015 he also received the Honorary Fellowship of the Royal Microscopical Society (Hon FRMS)<ref name="RMS">{{cite web | title=Honorary Fellows | website=RMS | url=https://www.rms.org.uk/membership/honorary-fellows.html | access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref> and the [[National Institute for Materials Science]] (NIMS) Award.<ref>[http://www.nims.go.jp/eng/news/press/2015/06/201504270.html NIMS Award]</ref>

In 2020 he received the [[Kavli Prize]] in Nanoscience (together with [[Harald Rose]] and [[Knut Urban]] and [[Ondrej Krivanek]]).<ref>[http://kavliprize.org/prizes-and-laureates/prizes/2020-kavli-prize-nanoscience 2020 Kavli Prize in Nanoscience], www.kavliprize.org. Retrieved 27 May 2020.</ref>
